title: Derived pullback on ringed topoi computed by K-flat resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the universe of the module sheaves, with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, equipped with a ring map $c:u^{-1}R\to S$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $K(R)$ be the homotopy category of cochain complexes of $R$-modules and $Q_R:K(R)\to D(R)$, $Q_S:K(S)\to D(S)$ the derived-category localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There is an exact left derived functor $Lu^*:D(R)\to D(S)$ with its canonical natural transformation $\epsilon:Lu^*Q_R\to Q_Su^*$ on $K(R)$. For every K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $\epsilon_P:Lu^*(Q_RP)\to Q_S(u^*P)$ is an isomorphism. Termwise pullback sends every quasi-isomorphism between such complexes to a quasi-isomorphism. Thus for any quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to A$ with $P$ K-flat with flat terms, the composite $Lu^*(Q_RA)\xrightarrow{Lu^*(Q_Rp)^{-1}}Lu^*(Q_RP)\xrightarrow{\epsilon_P}Q_S(u^*P)$ is an isomorphism, natural in maps of such resolutions and compatible with composition of the resulting comparisons.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Termwise module pullback induces an additive functor $T:K(R)\to K(S)$: an additive functor sends a chain homotopy $h$ to $u^*h$, preserving the identity $f-g=dh+hd$. It is exact on homotopy categories, since shifts and mapping cones are formed from finite direct sums and the differential matrices, which additive pullback preserves, including their signs. Put $F=Q_S\circ T:K(R)\to D(S)$; this is exact because localization sends each cone triangle to a distinguished triangle [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of K-flat complexes with flat terms. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism from an object of $\mathcal P$.

Let $s:P\to P'$ be a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes with flat terms. The forgetful functor from module sheaves to sheaves of sets preserves finite limits and reflects them, and preserves epimorphisms. For the latter assertion first forget to abelian-group sheaves, which preserves finite colimits because module sheafification commutes with forgetting; hence it preserves epimorphisms. Then use the characterization of epis of abelian-group sheaves as locally surjective maps. The natural underlying-sheaf isomorphism in [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] identifies the composite of $I.modules$ and the target forgetful functor with source forgetful followed by $u^{-1}$. Hence $I.modules$ preserves finite limits. Since $u^{-1}$ is a left adjoint it preserves epis; naturality of the same isomorphism and reflection of epis by target forgetting show that $I.modules$ preserves epis. Mathlib's preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels therefore gives preservation of cohomology and of quasi-isomorphisms by $I.modules$. Construct the additive scalar-extension functor $E_c$ from sectionwise extension of scalars followed by module sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For the identity coefficient map, the standard extension-of-scalars identity and the sheafification counit give a natural isomorphism $E_{id}\cong Id$. Identify the monoidal tensor-right functor with the site tensor-right functor using their common sheafification of the sectionwise tensor; this transports flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] to the predicate used in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback]. Apply that lemma with identity coefficient map and functor $E_{id}\circ I.modules$. Transport its K-flat conclusion along the natural identity-scalar-extension isomorphism, and use the specialization of independent-coefficient K-flatness to ordinary K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex], obtaining K-flatness of $I.modules(P)$ and $I.modules(P')$. Now [lem-pur-change-of-rings-kflat-quasi-iso] applied to $E_c$ sends the quasi-isomorphism $I.modules(s)$ to a quasi-isomorphism. The supplied object and morphism equations give a natural isomorphism between $uStar$ and $E_c\circ I.modules$, whose induced isomorphism of arrows transfers this conclusion to termwise $uStar(s)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] with $F=Q_S\circ T$ and the class $\mathcal P$. Its first hypothesis is step 1. Its second hypothesis holds because step 2 says $T(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Q_S$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $F(s)$ is an isomorphism. The criterion supplies an everywhere-defined exact left derived functor $Lu^*:D(R)\to D(S)$ with its canonical natural transformation $\epsilon:Lu^*\circ Q_R\to Q_S\circ T$ and an isomorphism $\epsilon_P$ for every $P\in\mathcal P$. Together with step 2 this proves the first two assertions.

For a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to A$ with $P\in\mathcal P$, define $\alpha_p=\epsilon_P\circ Lu^*(Q_Rp)^{-1}$. Both factors are invertible, by localization and step 3, so $\alpha_p:Lu^*(Q_RA)\to Q_S(TP)$ is the claimed isomorphism. For a map of resolutions $(a,b):(P\xrightarrow p A)\to(P'\xrightarrow {p'} A')$, the equality $p'a=bp$ implies $Lu^*(Q_Ra)\,Lu^*(Q_Rp)^{-1}=Lu^*(Q_Rp')^{-1}\,Lu^*(Q_Rb)$. Naturality of $\epsilon$ gives $Q_S(Ta)\epsilon_P=\epsilon_{P'}Lu^*(Q_Ra)$, hence $Q_S(Ta)\alpha_p=\alpha_{p'}Lu^*(Q_Rb)$. This proves naturality without requiring that a chain map between arbitrary resolutions be chosen. For two resolutions $p:P\to A$ and $q:Q\to A$, their comparison in $D(S)$ is $C_{q,p}=\alpha_q\alpha_p^{-1}$. If $qa=p$, the preceding equality gives $C_{q,p}=Q_S(Ta)$. For a third resolution $r$, $C_{r,q}C_{q,p}=\alpha_r\alpha_q^{-1}\alpha_q\alpha_p^{-1}=C_{r,p}$ and $C_{p,p}=\operatorname{id}$, proving compatibility with composition.
